title: Make the install.sh PATH check strictly bounded and keep the profile byte-identical on re-install
summary: The install.sh fix task was accepted, but the full change-set check of the 0.1.1 release rejected the result: the fresh-shell check is not strictly bounded (the watchdog writes predictable files in a shared temporary directory, ignores its own timeout status when deciding success, and can wait forever on a shell that ignores the soft kill signal), and a re-install over an existing profile leaves an extra blank line instead of keeping the rest of the file byte-identical. The fix must live in install.sh itself, with tests for each case, so the release can pass its full check and be published.
requirements: The fresh-shell check must be strictly bounded in time: when the bound elapses, the checked shell is stopped (a graceful signal first, a forceful stop after a short grace period) and the check counts as failed.

The timeout status must take part in the success decision. Success only when the path reported by the fresh login shell for forgel-code exactly matches the launcher path just written. Any other case, including a timed-out shell, is a failure.
The failure report names the edited profile file, the login shell that was checked, the PATH block that was written and the PATH the fresh shell reported.

Temporary files used by the check live in a private directory that other users cannot read, with unpredictable names, and are removed on every outcome; after the check finishes no file and no process from it is left behind.

A re-install must leave the rest of the profile byte-identical: repeated installs do not accumulate blank lines, and dropping the block restores the file content exactly as it was before the block was added, including the trailing-newline state.
install.sh stays POSIX sh and keeps working without GNU coreutils timeout, on macOS and Linux.

Existing behaviour is preserved: login shell detection, profile selection, FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE and FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH opt-outs, idempotent --uninstall (including ~/.bashrc and FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE), --help and exit code 2 for an unknown argument.
Every fixed defect gets a test in the repository test suite; no existing test may be weakened to make the suite pass.
acceptance: A check against a shell that never answers and ignores the graceful stop signal ends within a bounded time with a non-zero status and a report naming the profile file and the observed PATH.
The shell-inspection test finishes, leaves no stray process and leaves no temporary file behind.
Installing twice over the same profile produces a file byte-identical to the file after the first install; dropping the block restores the original content exactly.
The full test suite of the repository passes, including the existing installer, shell-detection, opt-out, uninstall and packaging tests.
Temporary files created by the check are not readable by other users and are gone after both a successful and a failed check.
constraints: POSIX sh only; no dependency on GNU coreutils.
No new documented environment variables; existing variables keep their meaning.
Keep the current verification bound unless a documented reason forces a different value.
User-facing output in English, matching the existing installer tone.
assumptions: The whole fix stays inside install.sh and its tests; the client package and CHANGELOG are untouched.
The verification bound stays at its current value; no new environment variable is added for it.
The private temporary location is created under the system temporary directory with owner-only permissions and removed on every exit path.
The release of the installer fix is re-checked and published by the normal release process after the fix is accepted; no version or tag is chosen here.
